clue.text: Do some needling, upsetting bored emir

indicators.note: upsetting the words bored emir throws their letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone doing needlework annoys a bored Middle Eastern ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Needling' suggests teasing someone, but here it is literal work with a needle.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroider is to decorate cloth with stitches, which is needlework.

clue.text: One praising former bellringer?

parts.note: ex means former
a toller rings a bell

explanation.surface: A retired bell-ringer described as someone giving praise.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise highly, so one who extols is a praiser.

clue.text: Poor brandy is regularly thrown away

indicators.note: regularly thrown away means every other letter of brandy is discarded, leaving the first, third and fifth

explanation.surface: Cheap brandy keeps being poured away.
explanation.definitionFit: Bad and poor are synonyms meaning of low quality.

clue.text: Toxic gas round area

parts.note: O is round in shape
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: Poisonous gas spreading around a district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone, a form of oxygen, is a toxic gas at ground level.

clue.text: Democrat is getting put into post. Sad.

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics
appointing someone puts them into a post

explanation.surface: A tweet-style complaint about a Democrat's appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: The terse 'Sad.' mimics a political tweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disappointing is regrettable or unfortunate, which is one sense of sad.

clue.text: Unfortunately nastier type of Greek wine

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests the letters of nastier have gone awry and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sadly rather nasty Greek wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Taking shilling off self-satisfied fool

indicators.note: taking a letter off a word means removing it; here the shilling abbreviation goes
with taking, off signals that a letter is removed from the following word

parts.note: self-satisfied means smug
S is the abbreviation for a shilling, an old British coin

explanation.surface: A smug fool loses a shilling.
explanation.walkthrough: A shilling was a pre-decimal British coin, abbreviated S.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug is British slang for a gullible person, a dupe or fool.

clue.text: Promoting after-hours activity of teachers around Eton — not on

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: teachers do marking of homework in the evenings

indicators.note: not on means the letters of on are dropped from the school name

parts.note: Eton is a famous English public school

explanation.surface: Teachers at Eton advertising their work outside hours.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is a famous English boarding school; 'not on' strips two letters from it, and 'around' wraps the teachers' evening task round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Marketing is advertising and selling a product, which is promoting it.

clue.text: Good line to develop

parts.note: a row is a line

explanation.surface: A good course of action for improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow is to increase or mature, a synonym for develop.

clue.text: Running outside is boring

indicators.note: running, as of colours or dye, suggests the word outside is mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Going for a run outdoors is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running outside' reads as jogging; 'Running' is the anagram signal on OUTSIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tedious is dull and wearisome, which is a synonym of boring.

clue.text: Trunk with entangled roots

indicators.note: entangled says the letters of roots are twisted up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tree trunk with tangled roots.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk of the body is the torso, the part without head or limbs.

clue.text: Very big poplar gets cut down

indicators.note: a poplar being cut down suggests the phrase is sliced so a run of letters is left inside

explanation.surface: A huge poplar tree is felled.
explanation.definitionFit: Large means of great size, a synonym of very big.

clue.text: Act as MP for about now?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the present is now

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone is acting as an MP for now.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP speaks for constituents in Parliament, so represents them.

clue.text: Enquire too intrusively about diamonds being expensive

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to pry is to enquire too intrusively
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Nosy questions about costly diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Pricey is an informal word for costly or dear.

clue.text: Example of popular position

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a stance is a position or posture

explanation.surface: A case of a widely held opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or example of something.

clue.text: Look forward to speech: spit it out!

definitions.note: an exclamation describing the act, whereas the answer names that act as a noun

parts.note: to look forward to something is to expect it
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: An impatient listener urges a hesitant speaker to get on with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spit it out!' is said to someone hesitating, but here it is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectoration is coughing up and spitting phlegm, literally spitting it out.

clue.text: Fortress — it's captured by rogue with the Spanish

indicators.note: captured by says the first word is held inside the other piece

parts.note: a cad is a rogue or scoundrel
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A stronghold taken by a scoundrel with Spanish allies.
explanation.definitionFit: A citadel is a fortress guarding a city.

clue.text: Stamped like eggs can be?

definitions.meaning: a path stamped flat by feet is a ... track
eggs are often whisked or whipped before cooking

explanation.surface: Something trampled down, compared to whipped eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A beaten path is trodden down, and beaten eggs have been whisked.

clue.text: One with unpleasant views returning to Gibraltar

indicators.note: returning says the pieces to and the short Gibraltar are read backwards

parts.note: Gib is the common short form of Gibraltar, the British territory at the tip of Spain; that the reversed letters also sit in the printed text is a coincidence, since no word signals hiding

explanation.surface: A prejudiced person heading back to Gibraltar.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft read this as a hidden word, but nothing signals hiding: 'to' plus GIB, the usual short name for Gibraltar, is reversed by 'returning'.
explanation.definitionFit: A bigot holds intolerant, prejudiced opinions, which are unpleasant views.

clue.text: Foundation degree son is chasing

indicators.note: chasing puts the son and is pieces behind the degree, as if running after it

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A son goes after a foundation degree, a UK two-year qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foundation degree' reads as one phrase, a British vocational qualification, but 'Foundation' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A basis is the underlying support for something, its foundation.

clue.text: Impatient desire to behead a sorceress

indicators.note: behead means the first letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: a witch is a sorceress

explanation.surface: Someone longing to execute a witch.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is a restless craving or eager longing for something.

clue.text: Daughter's after sentimentally pretty fabric

indicators.note: after puts the daughter abbreviation behind the other piece

parts.note: twee means sweet or pretty in a sentimental way

explanation.surface: A daughter chooses cloth that is a bit too cute.
explanation.definitionFit: Tweed is a rough woollen cloth, a kind of fabric.

clue.text: Diabetic treatment mostly degrading when temperature's out

indicators.note: out says the temperature abbreviation is removed
mostly says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: insulting means degrading or demeaning

explanation.surface: A medicine that spoils when the heat is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts INSULTING to INSULTIN; removing T leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the hormone injected by diabetics to control blood sugar.

clue.text: Initially leave England an open country

indicators.note: initially says take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Departing England first for open land.
explanation.definitionFit: A lea is a meadow or grassy field, open country in poetry.

clue.text: Boater, perhaps, that's wasting time

indicators.note: wasting time means losing the abbreviation for time from the word

explanation.surface: A straw boater, regarded as a waste of time.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat straw hat, not a sailor; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a stiff flat-crowned straw headwear, one example of the answer.

clue.text: Member is arriving after time to enact law

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member of the body
arriving after the due time means being late

explanation.surface: A Member of Parliament turns up late to pass legislation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' suggests a Member of Parliament, but it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make or pass laws, which is enacting law.
